headline: Elon Musk posted a screenshot of his Grok Bot AI assistant ordering Lego for him that showed the order number, shipping and billing addresses and the last four digits of his payment card.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the Ynetnews headline overstates it, because only the last four card digits showed and no breach of Grok or Lego is reported, so the weight is Musk's own post exposing checkout details.
importance_line: What changed is that Musk's own showcase of Grok Bot shopping exposed checkout details, which matters first to shoppers deciding whether to give an AI agent their card, then to xAI, Musk's AI company, and the doubt is that no breach of Grok or Lego is reported, Musk says the address is not his home, and the claim that his order was cancelled is not confirmed.
summary: Raw Story and Fashion Times UK report that Musk posted a screenshot on 11 Oct 2026 of Grok Bot, his AI shopping assistant, ordering five Lego Star Wars sets for $241.34, and that it showed the order number, a shipping and a billing address and the last four digits of an American Express card; Musk replied that he does not live at that address because it is where his security team receives mail. This follows his 10 Oct 2026 post telling users to photograph their credit cards so Grok could shop for them, which our 11 Oct 2026 edition carried from Moneycontrol, and what is new today is that his own demonstration exposed the kind of data that advice invites.
notes: Read Raw Story and Fashion Times UK in full; the Ynetnews pool item (https://www.ynetnews.com/tech-and-digital/article/b1bfjwksfe) carried only a short standfirst, so it is not the credited source. Follow-up of the 11 Oct 2026 edition item on Moneycontrol (pool id 1011:C02-02).
